description: Start a supervised command using run_command's native sandbox and approval rules. Poll or cancel the handle. Final delivery requires every handle to be terminal.

propertyDescriptions.executionScope: Default workspace sandbox. Request host only for an explicit per-command host escalation approved with this invocation. Benchmark remains container-confined.
propertyDescriptions.requiredCapabilities: Compatibility requirements only, never permission grants. test/verify assumes loopback_tcp for runtime IPC. Set [] for checks known not to need IPC. Separate sandbox commands may not share localhost; keep server and client under one supervised command. Missing capabilities require explicit approval for host execution; Benchmark never escapes.
propertyDescriptions.program: Executable name, path relative to cwd, or absolute local executable. Same resolution and isolation as run_command.
propertyDescriptions.args: Literal structured argv, including multiline code. For cmd /c the complete command must be one argument; no automatic shell-string joining.
propertyDescriptions.cwd: Normal CLI workspace: /workspace or a relative path; other Linux container directories are allowed. Host scope/Full access uses host paths. Benchmark keeps its offline worker paths.
propertyDescriptions.intent: Declared command purpose, not permission. Use test, build or verify for validation.
propertyDescriptions.verificationKind: Optional validation category. Missing verify/test categories default to custom; build defaults to build. Inapplicable or invalid metadata is normalized without blocking execution.
propertyDescriptions.timeoutMs: An optional hard process-lifetime limit. When omitted, the independent background lifetime limit applies instead of run_command's foreground timeout. Runtime returns the effective capped budget across later polls.
propertyDescriptions.reason: A concise explanation of why this command is needed for the current task.

guidance: Use for a long-running build, test, verification, install or server, with the same flat contract and network rules as run_command. A running handle confirms process startup, not application readiness; check readiness separately before dependent commands. Prefer direct test output over a filtering pipeline; Runtime returns execution status separately from validation passed/failed/unknown. After status running, use poll_command for bounded waits and cancel_command when no longer needed. Stop a server when its dependent work is done. Do not complete the task before observing every handle's terminal result. Missing validation metadata is normalized once, and remains attached across polls.
